DOCUMENTATION GAP in the proof chain: region2d's docstring asserts that the verdict is constant on each (beta-cell x t-cell), but notes/lemmas.md proves Lemma B only at fixed t (plus a remark that the roles can be swapped). The two-parameter statement actually used (Hurwitz-ness is constant on any connected open subset of {D != 0, Delta_{m-1} != 0}) and the openness argument that justifies deciding only full-dimensional cells (SFP set is open, so a nonempty SFP set meets some sector; Lemma O in lemma_F_reduction.md) are not written down as the step that makes the CAD sound. Both follow verbatim from the written proofs (Rouché in (beta,t) + connectedness; strict inequalities), so this is a gap in the write-up, not in the mathematics.

REPLAY INDEPENDENCE is weaker than the docstring suggests: replay_counts checks (i) a sign change of the sympy-supplied basis factor f on each interval and (ii) per-polynomial distinct-root counts via the Descartes counter, but never checks that f divides the polynomial the interval is attributed to, and the squarefree part comes from sympy's dup_sqf_part. It is independent of the VAS isolator (as claimed), not of sympy. Tamper tests show it does catch a dropped, duplicated, shifted or misattributed interval (misattribution only via the count).

REPORTING ARTIFACTS in certificates (no effect on verdicts): `beta_critical` lists every root of the joint isolation on the hull [lo_r, hi_r], which includes roots outside the positivity cell -- 2,534 records carry a degenerate critical value `2` (it is the root of lc_L = beta - 2 whenever the hull starts at 2), and 6,777 degree-1 projection roots are recorded this way; `positivity_cells` endpoints and `beta_cell` bounds are isolating-interval ends (inner hulls), not the algebraic roots. Anyone reading the files as 'the critical values of this graph' will be misled.

VERDICT PRECEDENCE: region2d returns `stable_somewhere` whenever any cell is stable, even if other cells are undecided, so the tally's `escalate: 0` does not by itself show the 4 stable records have no undecided cells. I checked the 4 stored certificates directly: 0 undecided cells, every cell crosscheck=True (idx 1000255 and 1424629: 8 cells, 2 stable; 1387528: 1 cell, stable; K6 idx 1540943: 1 cell, stable). No effect at n=6, but the aggregate claim rests on that direct check rather than on the tally.

ROBUSTNESS BY ACCIDENT: the main loop never refines a first isolating interval that starts exactly at the hull end (unlike fastregion._cells); it only asserts cell_lo < cell_hi (loud failure, errors=0 in the sweep). That it never fired is because lc_L = beta - 2 is always in the projection set, so its degenerate (2,2) interval forces sympy's strict mode to separate every other interval from 2; likewise L's root exactly at t_min forces separation in t. If L were ever dropped from the curve set this would become a loud error, not a silent one. Also the hull logic (k_start = pos_pos[0], k_end = pos_pos[-1]) depends on sympy 1.14.0 returning intervals sorted and including roots exactly at inf/sup -- both verified here, but undocumented sympy behaviour.
checks_passed: (a) Projection set, read line by line: curves = {D (linear in t), Delta_{m-1} (Berkowitz det of the (m-1)x(m-1) Hurwitz matrix of p = phi + t*omega with c_k = coefficient of mu^{m-k}), L}. Delta is split into Q-irreducible factors (squarefree basis; multiplicities dropped), t-degree-0 factors become vertical lines in the projection; then the curve set is made pairwise coprime (gcd split, with vertical quotients moved to the projection); for every remaining curve the leading coefficient in t (covers the content of D = g*(d'+t s') since lc_D = s) and, for t-degree >= 2, the discriminant (asserted nonzero) are added; resultants in t of ALL pairs (including with L and D) are added, a zero resultant raises. This is exactly the Collins/McCallum bivariate projection: lc and disc give delineability of each squarefree curve over each open beta-cell, pairwise resultants forbid crossings, L-resultants forbid any root function crossing t_min(beta), so sectors above L are sign-invariant for every curve; degree drops (lc roots) and vertical lines are cell boundaries, excluded as measure-zero.

(a) Independent check that the curves are the right polynomials: at 96 random rational (beta,t) on 12 random graphs, region2d's symbolic D and Delta_5 equal eps^6 * c_6 and eps^{15} * Delta_5 of ctln.charpoly(-I+W_sigma) exactly, and equal den^5 * fastregion.hurwitz_det_poly; the vanishing/sign pattern of Hurwitz minors is invariant under the mu -> mu/eps scaling (factor eps^{k(k+1)/2} > 0), so the crosscheck against analyze_support is meaningful and three-valued-consistent.

Mathematical verdict on the CAD: the projection set {a_i, o_k, lc_t of every coprime curve, disc_t of every Q-irreducible factor of Delta_{m-1} with t-degree >= 2, pairwise resultants of all curves including D and L, vertical factors} is sufficient for sign-invariance of every curve on each (open beta-cell) x (t-sector above L), and the verdict is constant there by the (beta,t)-version of Lemma B (D = p(0) and Delta_{m-1} are the only loci where a root of the monic p can reach the imaginary axis; Rouché + connectedness). Points on curves are never SFP (strict conditions) and the SFP set is open, so a nonempty SFP region meets a full-dimensional sector and is found at that sector's sample; conversely a stable sample certifies its whole sector. Restriction to the positivity cells is sound by Lemma A.2. The code implements this faithfully; the first/last cells and the legal boundary are handled correctly (L is a curve, t_min(beta) is its root function, cells below it are illegal, cells above are sampled, roots exactly at 2 and at t_min are filtered). decide_point is three-valued and re-samples. The Descartes replay is correct (fuzzed) and catches tampering.

No contradiction between any cell verdict and ctln.analyze_support was found: 9,300 exact random points on 27 graphs (3 counterexamples, 20 dense-biased survivors, 4 vertical-factor cases, many-cell cases), each located in its exact CAD cell including points inside isolating intervals, 0 disagreements, 0 sector-count mismatches, 0 undecided; all 592 SFP points lie in cells marked stable and none outside the positivity set.

audits.details:
Independent re-derivation done entirely in sympy from the definition of W (no region2d.py/fastregion.py code used), exact rational/algebraic arithmetic in every decision. Scratch scripts and logs (re-runnable in order): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-CLTN/083b78b8-b6de-5340-9343-2e5fdd9085d8/scratchpad/wf_audit/idx1387528/{sturm_tools.py, stage1_build.py, stage2_positivity.py, stage3_hurwitz_cells.py, stage4_cells.py, stage5_limit.py, stage6_compare.py, stage7_extra.py} with stage*.log, stage1.pkl, stage3_crit.pkl, stage2.json.

Method. With eps=1/(t+1), delta=(beta-1)eps: (t+1)(I-W) = N = K + tJ, K = -(beta-1)I + beta(J - A^T). Because J is rank one, adj(N)·1 = adj(K)·1 is t-free and det N = D0(beta) + t·s(beta) with s = sum a_i; so x_i = (t+1)a_i(beta)/D(beta,t). a_0 = beta^4-3beta^3+4beta^2-2beta+1, a_1 = -(beta^3-3beta^2+2beta-1), a_2 = (beta-1)^2(beta^2-beta+1), a_3 = (beta-1)(beta^3-2beta^2+beta-1), a_4 = beta^2-beta+1, a_5 = -(beta^5-3beta^4+3beta^3-3beta^2+2beta-1). Positivity therefore reduces to beta in (2, beta_1') plus D>0, and D>0 holds on the whole legal half-line since (beta-2)D0+s = E(beta) > 0 there. Stability of -I+W is equivalent to Hurwitz stability of det(uI+N) (u=(t+1)s). I computed Delta_1..Delta_6 (Delta_6 = D·Delta_5), then a McCallum/Collins-style projection in beta (leading coefficients, discriminants, resultant with the legal boundary (beta-2)t-1, content) and counted real roots with my own Sturm-sequence counter (cross-checked against sympy's isolator). No projection polynomial has a root in (2, beta_1'), so the interval is one cell; exact sampling at five rational betas (one within 1e-8 of beta_1') shows zero legal t-roots and positive sign for every D, Delta_k. Result: the full-support stable set is exactly {2 < beta < beta_1', t > 1/(beta-2)}, equivalently 1 < q < (beta_1'-1)(1-eps); beta_1' = unique real root of beta^5-3beta^4+3beta^3-3beta^2+2beta-1 (irreducible), isolating interval (152/73, 25/12), ~2.0830248035. This matches the certificate's beta_critical minpoly exactly. For beta >= beta_1' no legal parameter gives a positive fixed point (a_5 <= 0 < a_2), so 'never stable' there holds irrespective of Hurwitz; informationally, Hurwitz itself persists past beta_1' (Delta_5 first vanishes on the legal boundary at ~2.09736, the degree-20 LC-43 polynomial in the certificate, which I reproduced as res_t(Delta_5, (beta-2)t-1); the t->oo limit Hurwitz condition persists to ~2.14055). The t->oo limit (P = P0 + tP1, P1 = 1^T adj(uI+K)1) is Hurwitz-stable on both sides of beta_1', and the limit positivity is the same t-free a_i, so the limit boundary coincides with beta_1' and is the positivity (a_5) boundary. Independent confirmations: exact Lyapunov-equation positive-definiteness at four points (and failure at a control point beyond the Hurwitz boundary), ctln.analyze_support at 11 legal points including the report's witness, and a float sanity grid with zero violations.

The only defect found is in the write-up/serialization: the stated interval (152/73, 27/13) for beta_1' (REPORT_n6.md line 121 and the task text) is misordered and 27/13 is actually below beta_1'; the certificate's cell endpoints 27/13 (positivity cell) and 152/73 (stable cell) are rational isolating-interval lower endpoints standing in for the algebraic root and, read literally, under-cover the true region (2, beta_1') and contradict each other. The mathematical claim 'stable iff 2 < beta < beta_1' at every legal t; never stable for beta >= beta_1'' is fully confirmed.

Method prepared for the spot-check (ready to run, ~15 min on 4 cores once features.jsonl completes): for each selected graph, 300 points = {beta = 2+1/k, k in 2..10000} x {t = 1e2..1e9} (beta -> 2+, t large), {beta = 2+1/k} x {t = (1+1/j)/(beta-2), j up to 1e8} (legality boundary q -> 1+), and 13 beta values inside each of the graph's own positivity cells (incl. 1/1000 of the width from each endpoint) x 6 values of t from (1+1e-6)/(beta-2) to 1e8/(beta-2); eps = 1/(t+1), delta = (beta-1) eps, legality asserted, then ctln.analyze_support; any stable_fixed_point or BOUNDARY record is kept in full. No stable point or interval on a 'never' graph has been found, but the adversarial search itself has not yet been executed, so the 'never' verdicts remain unverified by this audit beyond the spectral check on 9,834 survivors.
